questions.questionText: Which component performs most arithmetic and logical operations in a computer?
questions.explanation: The central processing unit executes instructions and performs arithmetic and logical operations.

curriculum.objective: Explain how hardware components, operating systems and input-output devices work together to meet user requirements.

questions.questionText: Why is RAM described as volatile memory?
options: It can only store video files
Its contents are lost when power is removed
It is slower than magnetic tape
Its contents can never be changed
questions.correctAnswer: Its contents are lost when power is removed
questions.explanation: RAM requires continuous electrical power to retain its current data, so stored contents disappear when power is removed.

curriculum.objective: Explain how hardware components, operating systems and input-output devices work together to meet user requirements.

questions.questionText: A designer needs to print large architectural drawings accurately. Which output device is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A large-format plotter produces precise line drawings on paper sizes suitable for architectural plans.

curriculum.objective: Explain how hardware components, operating systems and input-output devices work together to meet user requirements.

questions.questionText: A school replaces hard drives with solid-state drives in laptops. Which combined effect is most likely?
options: Slower access and higher mechanical wear
More moving parts and greater noise
Faster access and better shock resistance
questions.correctAnswer: Faster access and better shock resistance
questions.explanation: SSDs have no moving parts, so they generally access data faster and resist physical shock better than hard disks.

curriculum.objective: Explain how hardware components, operating systems and input-output devices work together to meet user requirements.

questions.questionText: How many different values can one byte represent?
questions.explanation: A byte contains eight bits, so it can represent 2⁸ = 256 distinct binary patterns.

curriculum.objective: Represent and convert text, number, image and sound data while explaining how resolution and encoding affect quality and size.

questions.questionText: What is decimal 13 in binary?
questions.explanation: Decimal 13 equals 8 + 4 + 1, producing binary place values 1101.

curriculum.objective: Represent and convert text, number, image and sound data while explaining how resolution and encoding affect quality and size.

questions.questionText: If the color depth of an image increases while all other factors stay fixed, what usually happens?
options: Fewer colors appear and file size increases
Resolution falls but storage is unchanged
More colors are possible and file size increases
The image becomes vector graphics automatically
questions.correctAnswer: More colors are possible and file size increases
questions.explanation: Greater color depth uses more bits per pixel, allowing more colors but requiring more storage.

curriculum.objective: Represent and convert text, number, image and sound data while explaining how resolution and encoding affect quality and size.

questions.questionText: Uncompressed stereo audio is sampled at 44,000 samples per second with 16 bits per sample. Approximately how many bits are stored per second?
questions.explanation: The bit rate is 44,000 × 16 × 2 channels = 1,408,000 bits per second.

curriculum.objective: Represent and convert text, number, image and sound data while explaining how resolution and encoding affect quality and size.

questions.questionText: Which device forwards data packets between different networks?
questions.explanation: A router examines addressing information and forwards packets between separate networks.

curriculum.objective: Explain network components, protocols and security controls and apply them to common connectivity and threat scenarios.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of HTTPS when accessing a website?
options: Guarantee every page is factually correct
Encrypt data exchanged with the site
questions.correctAnswer: Encrypt data exchanged with the site
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt data in transit and authenticate the server, reducing interception and tampering risks.

curriculum.objective: Explain network components, protocols and security controls and apply them to common connectivity and threat scenarios.

questions.questionText: Which control most directly reduces damage if a password is stolen?
questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication requires another verified factor, so a stolen password alone is less likely to grant access.

curriculum.objective: Explain network components, protocols and security controls and apply them to common connectivity and threat scenarios.

questions.questionText: An employee receives an urgent email linking to a fake sign-in page. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: The attacker impersonates a trusted sender and uses a deceptive page to capture the employee’s credentials.

curriculum.objective: Explain network components, protocols and security controls and apply them to common connectivity and threat scenarios.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a primary key in a database table?
options: Store every field as an image
questions.explanation: A primary key has a unique value for each row, allowing every record to be identified reliably.

curriculum.objective: Design and query simple data structures and databases while applying validation, integrity and backup principles.

questions.questionText: Which validation rule best checks that an exam mark is from 0 to 100?
questions.explanation: A range check verifies that a numeric value lies between specified minimum and maximum limits.

curriculum.objective: Design and query simple data structures and databases while applying validation, integrity and backup principles.

questions.questionText: Which SQL query returns all students whose score is at least 70?
questions.explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows, and >= includes scores equal to or greater than 70.

curriculum.objective: Design and query simple data structures and databases while applying validation, integrity and backup principles.

questions.questionText: A database stores the same customer address in many order rows. Which design improvement best reduces update anomalies?
options: Repeat the address in additional columns
Remove every primary and foreign key
Convert all fields into one long text value
Separate customers and orders into related tables
questions.correctAnswer: Separate customers and orders into related tables
questions.explanation: Normalization separates customer data from order data and links the tables, reducing repeated values and inconsistent updates.

curriculum.objective: Design and query simple data structures and databases while applying validation, integrity and backup principles.

questions.questionText: Which feature most improves accessibility for a user who cannot see images?
questions.explanation: Alternative text communicates an image’s purpose to screen readers and users who cannot view it.

questions.questionText: Why should a developer use test data at boundary values?
options: To guarantee the program has no defects
To reveal errors at accepted limits
To replace all normal test cases
questions.correctAnswer: To reveal errors at accepted limits
questions.explanation: Boundary testing checks values at and around permitted limits, where comparison and validation errors often occur.

questions.questionText: A school collects student birth dates for account verification. Which practice follows data minimization?
options: Keep every possible personal detail forever
Publish the data for unrestricted reuse
Collect only data necessary for the stated purpose
Share all records with unrelated advertisers
questions.correctAnswer: Collect only data necessary for the stated purpose
questions.explanation: Data minimization means limiting collection and retention to information genuinely needed for a defined purpose.

questions.questionText: A team uses an online photograph in a commercial app. What should it verify first?
options: The file has the largest dimensions
The photographer uses the same device
The image appears in a search result
The license permits the intended reuse
questions.correctAnswer: The license permits the intended reuse
questions.explanation: Copyright applies even when an image is easy to find online, so the team must confirm licensing permits its planned use.
